perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s available perspective:

- Christian knows Jonathan Balogun as his childhood best friend, someone he often seeks advice from and whose more educated perspective he values.
- Christian had been feeling that Jonathan was hiding something important; this made him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop and confronted him about the feeling.
- Christian heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something from him, that he was in some trouble, and that he hadn’t known how to tell him.
- Christian told Jonathan he was worried, offered to help, and said they could face it together. Jonathan replied that the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe and told Jonathan that Jonathan was being framed and someone was trying to set him up.
- Christian heard Jonathan ask if he was sure and who would do such a thing. Christian said he wasn’t sure yet, but had leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him and said he didn’t know what he would do without him.
- Christian then came to believe/found out that the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute.
- Christian told Jonathan that he had found out who was behind it—someone they both know and trust—and planned to confront them and bring them to justice. Jonathan expressed disbelief, warned that the person was dangerous, and said he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- Christian’s own actions available to him include: arranging the coffee shop meeting, confronting Jonathan, offering help, asking about possible illegal activity, investigating discreetly, gathering evidence, and planning to confront the culprit.
- The specific identity/name of the culprit is not stated in the dialogue available to Christian here.
